reviews.title: WIDGET LAGS!!!
reviews.text: In the free version, you can’t subtract glasses of water. Suspiciously, the widget also lags 5 seconds before updating. Definitely not trying to get you to double click and then only be able to fix it by paying $$ for a subscription. That’d be uncool.

reviews.title: Functional but
reviews.text: Even the paid version has ads for this company’s other apps and solicitation for “donuts” for the creators. I would not recommend this app, not because it doesn’t track water consumption, but because of these non functional annoyances.

reviews.title: Paying for Basic Features
reviews.text: The fact that I have to pay 40 bucks just to tell the app that I drank milk is crazy to me. Basic features shouldn’t be locked behind such a big paywall.

reviews.title: Everything paywalled
reviews.text: There’s a ton of features and lots of useful interactions, but clicking anything but water will bring up a subscription page.

reviews.title: Cannot choose size for cup of milk
reviews.text: It prompted me to buy even before I have a chance to try for a few days.

reviews.title: Problems after iOS27 update
reviews.text: The only reason I updated to iOS 27 was because the app kept crashing on me in iOS18. Before I updated to iOS 27 I tried 26 first. The app continued to crash on me every single time I tried to input anything. Now that I updated iOS 27, I can’t update the temperature portion of the hydration goal screen, which is vital to proper hydration. This app has been nothing but frustration lately. I cannot recommend it.

reviews.title: If you have an eating disorder, don’t download this app!
reviews.text:
And I would also suggest that you read this even if you don’t have an eating disorder, before you decide whether or not you want to proceed with this. So, before I even start on my own issues with this app, let me explain why I raised the topic of eating disorders. 

I noticed a reviewer who had an eating disorder, who pointed out that some drinks are described as ‘evil’ in the app. This wasn’t the first complaint about that word. I’m beyond furious with the second half of the response by the team:
“We're sorry if [IF? That’s no way to start an apology! It should say ‘that it made’. ‘If’ implies that you don’t believe the reviewer!]… the labeling made you feel uncomfortable [UNCOMFORTABLE! Does the writer know anything at all about eating disorders?! It didn’t just make the reviewer uncomfortable, like they bought the wrong armchair. It set their recovery back considerably! They were very brave to raise this with the app owners, and even were kind enough to say lovely things about the app first!]—it's never our intention to set anyone back. We're all about promoting hydration and a balanced lifestyle [And clearly not all about how you affect people’s mental health]. Remember, the term "evil" is just a nudge to encourage healthier choices for overall well-being, the weight loss actually plays the least role in that. It's essential to focus on what makes you feel good, both physically and mentally.   
Feel free to do your own choices, and don't hesitate to consult with your doc

reviews.title: Promising, but..
reviews.text: The app seems promising at first, but since there are no alternative beverages beyond plain water in the free version, the free version isn’t worth using unless water is all you drink. I wish there were at least two or three alternatives that you could select in the free version, such as soda and coffee, to start shaping an idea of your intake habits and get a taste of the app’s ability to track these. As it is now, I’m too worried about not liking the feature or using it long term to be willing to purchase access to it.
